"Who are you?" said the Caterpillar

Three curious questions

  1. Does every Copilot pilot and agent we run have a FAIRA or FAIRA LITE? Version 2 of Queensland's AI governance policy took effect in August 2026.
  2. Who decides which teams can spend AI credits, and on which models? Cowork, Code, Autopilot and frontier models now run on usage-based billing.
  3. When our agents get their own identities, who owns them and how do we switch them off? Persistent agent identity is on the roadmap for November 2026, and UK NCSC advice calls for a tested way to stop agents.

Want to walk through any of this? Book 30 minutes with me, or reply to the email this came with.
Charlie Marie Shanks, AI Workforce Solutions Specialist, Microsoft

Sources for this issue

This is a summary of publicly available Microsoft announcements, blogs, the public AI at Work Roadmap and public government and media sources in Australia and the UK, compiled for Queensland public sector customers. It is not legal or licensing advice. Features roll out gradually and may differ by tenant, cloud and licence; roadmap dates are targets, not delivery commitments. Event times are shown as published (mostly US time).

Curiouser and Curiouser, Issue 03. Next issue in a fortnight. Issue 04 arrives on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The animated welcome plays on a computer or tablet.

How it works is based on Microsoft's 25 September 2026 announcement, Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot: everyday work on a fixed-cost user licence with Auto choosing the model; Cowork, Code, Autopilot and frontier models on usage-based credits; Agent 365 spend policies, credit approvals and model controls; and credit balances for users plus value insights for leaders. Some of these controls are still rolling out. No prices are shown; see Microsoft for current licensing.

This page sets no cookies and uses no tracking or analytics. It only remembers your display choices, and that you have seen the welcome and the tour, on your own device.
